social.title: Rays Baseball Back at Tropicana Field
social.description: The Rays are home again in St. Pete after a season away, under a repaired roof with a new video board and the catwalks still in play.
social.bonus: Touch the rays in the tank behind right-centre field before the game.

social.title: Lightning Night at Benchmark International Arena
social.description: The loudest building in the NHL when it's full, with a Tesla coil goal celebration and a downtown crowd that spills straight into Channelside afterwards.
social.bonus: Get there for warmups and stay for the organ. Both are part of it.

social.title: Bucs Sunday at Raymond James Stadium
social.description: A 65,000-seat stadium with a full-size pirate ship in the north end that fires its cannons on every score, and a tailgate scene that starts at dawn.
social.bonus: Be in the lot four hours early. That's where the actual event is.

social.title: Cigar City Pints at the Arena Taproom
social.description: Jai Alai IPA poured at the brewery's downtown taproom by the arena — the beer that put Tampa on the craft map, drunk where the crowds are.
social.bonus: Drink a Jai Alai and a Maduro back to back and pick your side.

social.title: Show Night at The Ritz Ybor
social.description: A 1917 cinema on 7th Avenue turned into Ybor's main room, with a balcony, a good floor and a calendar that runs from metal to house.
social.bonus: Watch the first two songs from the balcony, then go down to the floor.

social.title: The Speakeasy Behind the Laundromat
social.description: A working laundromat café on Central Avenue in St. Pete with a hidden door at the back that opens onto a Cuban-inflected speakeasy, Thursday to Sunday.
social.bonus: Order a coffee at the counter first and act like you don't know.

social.title: Bowl and Drink at Splitsville
social.description: Twelve lanes, billiards, shuffleboard and a tiki bar in Channelside, with sushi arriving at the lane while you're still bowling.
social.bonus: Play a full game where everyone bowls with their off hand.

social.title: Bar Crawl Down Ybor's 7th Avenue
social.description: One of only three National Historic Landmark districts in Florida, and on a Friday night it is six blocks of brick street, wrought iron and open doors.
social.bonus: Start at the east end and don't skip the smallest bar you pass.

social.title: Flamenco at Columbia Restaurant
social.description: Six nights a week a flamenco company performs in the Patio dining room of the 1905 building, with a $10 cover on top of dinner.
social.bonus: Book the 9:30 show and sit at the front. The footwork is the point.

social.title: Waterfront Sunset at Hula Bay
social.description: A marina-side bar and restaurant on Tyson Avenue with two full outdoor bars, boats pulling straight up to the dock, and the sun setting over the water.
social.bonus: Get a table on the outer deck and stay through the whole sunset.

social.title: Taproom Night at Coppertail
social.description: An independent production brewery and kitchen in a big Ybor warehouse, with a tap wall deep enough to make a flight a real decision.
social.bonus: Order the flight, rank them, and buy a crowler of the winner.

social.title: Sparkman Wharf Beer Garden
social.description: Shipping-container kitchens around a lawn of picnic tables on the Channelside waterfront, with a long bar and the cruise terminal right there.
social.bonus: Claim a table by the water before seven and hold it all evening.

culture.title: Tampa Museum of Art on the Riverwalk
culture.description: Greek and Roman antiquities alongside serious contemporary shows, in a cantilevered building that glows at night over Curtis Hixon Park.
culture.bonus: Walk round the outside after dark to see the lighting installation.

culture.title: The Dalí Museum, St. Petersburg
culture.description: The largest collection of Dalí outside Europe, in a concrete bunker wrapped in a free-form glass geodesic bubble on the St. Pete waterfront.
culture.bonus: Stand at the right distance from Gala Contemplating and watch it change.

culture.title: A Movie at Tampa Theatre
culture.description: A 1926 atmospheric movie palace with a ceiling of fake stars and gargoyles, still showing films nightly with the Mighty Wurlitzer played before them.
culture.bonus: Get there early enough to hear the organ. That's half the ticket.

culture.title: Chihuly Collection, St. Petersburg
culture.description: A purpose-built gallery for Dale Chihuly's blown glass on Central Avenue, lit so that the work does most of the talking.
culture.bonus: Find the ceiling installation and lie back far enough to see all of it.

culture.title: MOSI, the Museum of Science & Industry
culture.description: A big hands-on science museum in north Tampa with a planetarium and enough to do that two hours becomes four.
culture.bonus: Sit through a full planetarium show even if you think you're too old.

culture.title: Henry B. Plant Museum's Minarets
culture.description: The 1891 railroad hotel whose thirteen silver minarets are Tampa's skyline signature, with one wing kept exactly as the Gilded Age guests left it.
culture.bonus: Count all thirteen minarets from the far side of the river.

culture.title: Tampa Bay History Center
culture.description: Three floors on the Riverwalk covering twelve thousand years of the bay, from the Tocobaga to the cattle trade to the cigar boom.
culture.bonus: Go up to the top floor first and work your way down chronologically.

culture.title: Ybor City Museum State Park
culture.description: A former bakery telling the story of the cigar city built by Cuban, Spanish, Italian and Jewish immigrants, with restored casitas out the back.
culture.bonus: Take the casita tour and look at how small the whole house actually is.

8ball.title: Wildcard: Bridge to Bridge
8ball.description: Start at the Tampa end of the bay and get yourself to the far side of the Sunshine Skyway and back in one day, stopping at three places you've never been.
8ball.bonus: No interstate on the way back. Take the causeways and the beach roads.

8ball.title: Wildcard: Order What the Bartender Orders
8ball.description: Three bars in one night, and at each one you order whatever the person behind the bar says they drink when their shift ends.
8ball.bonus: No substitutions, no matter what they say.

chill.title: Florida Botanical Gardens
chill.description: Thirty free acres of tropical planting, wetland boardwalk and palm collections in Largo, quiet on a weekday morning.
chill.bonus: Do the wetland boardwalk loop first, before it warms up.

chill.title: Downtown Dunedin and the Pinellas Trail
chill.description: A walkable Gulf-coast main street with breweries, a marina and the Pinellas Trail running straight through the middle of it.
chill.bonus: Rent bikes and ride the trail north to Honeymoon Island and back.

chill.title: Sunset at Sunset Beach
chill.description: The southern tip of Treasure Island, wide and white and facing straight west, with drum circles some evenings and no high-rises in the way.
chill.bonus: Stay a full twenty minutes after the sun has gone. That's the good part.

chill.title: Weedon Island Preserve Boardwalk
chill.description: Three thousand acres of mangrove and estuary on the bay side of St. Pete, with a boardwalk, an observation tower and almost nobody on it.
chill.bonus: Climb the tower at high tide and pick out the paddling trail markers.

chill.title: Hop the Pirate Water Taxi All Day
chill.description: Fourteen stops along the Riverwalk, Channel District and Davis Islands on a pirate-themed boat, with one wristband and unlimited rides.
chill.bonus: Ride the whole loop once without getting off, just to see the order of it.

chill.title: Sunken Gardens, St. Petersburg
chill.description: A century-old garden built in a drained sinkhole fifteen feet below street level, with flamingos and banyans and a temperature noticeably cooler than the pavement.
chill.bonus: Find the oldest tree in the garden and read its plaque.

chill.title: Ballast Point Pier at Golden Hour
chill.description: A short municipal pier off South Tampa with a view straight up the bay to downtown and a café at the landward end.
chill.bonus: Walk to the very end and stay until the skyline lights come on.

chill.title: Afternoon in Hyde Park Village
chill.description: Brick streets, live oaks and an open green surrounded by independent shops and cafes in Tampa's prettiest old neighbourhood.
chill.bonus: Walk the surrounding streets and pick the bungalow you'd actually buy.

chill.title: Curtis Hixon Park in the Evening
chill.description: A downtown lawn on the river between the art museum and the university's minarets, with colour-changing bridges and people out until late.
chill.bonus: Sit on the steps down to the water and stay for the bridge light change.

chill.title: Sunset on Bayshore Boulevard
chill.description: The longest continuous sidewalk in the world — four and a half miles of balustrade along Hillsborough Bay, with the city on one side and open water on the other.
chill.bonus: Walk the full length one way and get a ride back. Don't turn around early.

foodie.title: Cuban Bread Warm at La Segunda
foodie.description: Eighteen thousand loaves a day since 1915, each one still topped with a palmetto leaf, from a fourth-generation Ybor bakery.
foodie.bonus: Buy a loaf straight off the rack and eat the end of it in the car park.

foodie.title: Deviled Crabs at Brocato's
foodie.description: A 1948 sandwich shop on Columbus Drive doing the croquette-shaped Tampa deviled crab that almost nowhere else still makes properly.
foodie.bonus: Get one deviled crab, one Cuban, and a stuffed potato. Share nothing.

foodie.title: The Original Cuban at Columbia Restaurant
foodie.description: Florida's oldest restaurant, open since 1905 and now filling an entire Ybor City block across fifteen dining rooms of hand-painted tile.
foodie.bonus: Order the 1905 Salad and watch them toss it at the table.

foodie.title: The Super Grouper at Frenchy's Rockaway
foodie.description: Grouper landed locally, fried, and eaten at a beach shack with your feet basically in the sand — voted the best version of the sandwich again in 2026.
foodie.bonus: Eat it outside at a table facing the Gulf, not indoors.

foodie.title: Weekend Brunch at Oxford Exchange
foodie.description: A bookshop, coffee bar, champagne counter and sunlit conservatory in one 1891 building across from the university's minarets — brunch here is an event.
foodie.bonus: Stay for afternoon tea in the Conservatory after you've eaten.

foodie.title: Graze the Heights Public Market
foodie.description: Twenty-two vendors under the roof of a restored 1910 streetcar warehouse on the Hillsborough River, plus four sit-down restaurants and a riverfront lawn.
foodie.bonus: Build a meal from four different stalls and eat it outside by the water.

foodie.title: Ramen at Ichi Koroshi
foodie.description: The Seminole Heights ramen counter opened by the crew from the city's much-missed original, running out of the Jug & Bottle kitchen.
foodie.bonus: Add the extra chashu. You will not regret the extra chashu.

foodie.title: Bib Gourmand at Rooster & the Till
foodie.description: A small Seminole Heights room that has quietly been the best cooking in Tampa for a decade, holding a Michelin Bib Gourmand for doing it at fair prices.
foodie.bonus: Order whatever the server says came in that morning.

foodie.title: Cuban Sandwich Crawl Down 7th Avenue
foodie.description: Ybor City invented the Tampa Cuban — no mayo, salami in the stack — and you can eat four versions of it in six blocks of brick street.
foodie.bonus: Rank them honestly at the end and defend your pick.

foodie.title: Native-Inspired Dinner at Ulele
foodie.description: A restored 1903 water works building beside the river, serving dishes built on Florida native ingredients with a spring-water brewery in the back.
foodie.bonus: Order the alligator hush puppies and the Ulele Spring Brewery flight.

foodie.title: Pour-Over at Buddy Brew, Hyde Park
foodie.description: The roaster that started Tampa's specialty coffee scene, in a small shop off the Hyde Park Village green where you can sit outside all morning.
foodie.bonus: Order a pour-over of the single origin and ask where the lot came from.

foodie.title: Bern's and the Harry Waugh Dessert Room
foodie.description: A South Howard steakhouse with the largest restaurant wine collection in the world, then upstairs to 48 private booths built out of old wine casks for dessert.
foodie.bonus: Take the kitchen and cellar tour between courses. They will actually do it.

adventure.title: Tandem Jump at Skydive City Z-Hills
adventure.description: A 13,500-foot exit over the flat green grid of Pasco County at one of the busiest and most respected drop zones in the world, running for over thirty years.
adventure.bonus: Stay for a beer at the bar afterwards and watch the next load land.

adventure.title: Upper Tampa Bay Trail
adventure.description: Seven flat miles of rail-trail through pine flatwoods and over tidal creeks on the north-west side of the city, quiet enough to hear the birds.
adventure.bonus: Ride out to the far trailhead and back without stopping for water.

adventure.title: Fish the Skyway Pier
adventure.description: The old Sunshine Skyway roadway, cut off and left standing in the middle of Tampa Bay as the longest fishing pier in the world, open around the clock.
adventure.bonus: Rent a rod, fish till dark, and watch the new bridge light up above you.

adventure.title: Sunset Sail off Clearwater Beach
adventure.description: Out through Clearwater Pass onto the Gulf on a catamaran as the sun drops, usually with dolphins working the boat's wake on the way back in.
adventure.bonus: Get up on the trampoline netting at the bow for the last twenty minutes.

adventure.title: Manatees at the TECO Viewing Center
adventure.description: Hundreds of manatees crowd into the warm-water discharge canal of a power station every winter, watched free from a boardwalk a few metres above them.
adventure.bonus: Climb the observation tower and count how many you can see at once.

adventure.title: Bike the Tampa Riverwalk End to End
adventure.description: Two and a half miles of continuous waterfront path from Armature Works to the Channel District, past parks, museums and a working river.
adventure.bonus: Ride it once each way and stop at a different spot on the way back.

adventure.title: Zipline the Courses at TreeHoppers
adventure.description: Central Florida's largest aerial adventure park: eight courses, over a hundred elements, ziplines and rope bridges strung through live oaks an hour north of the city.
adventure.bonus: Finish the hardest course you qualify for, then go back and do it faster.

adventure.title: Kayak the Fort De Soto Paddling Trail
adventure.description: Two and a half miles of marked trail through mangrove tunnels and seagrass flats in a 1,100-acre park at the mouth of Tampa Bay.
adventure.bonus: Get into the narrowest mangrove tunnel you can find and go quiet.

adventure.title: Ferry to Caladesi Island
adventure.description: A short boat from Honeymoon Island to one of the last completely undeveloped barrier islands in Florida — no bridge, no road, three miles of empty sand.
adventure.bonus: Walk the full length of the beach until you stop seeing other footprints.

adventure.title: Paddle the Hillsborough with Canoe Escape
adventure.description: A self-guided run down a blackwater river through cypress and oak with alligators on the banks, dropped in and picked up by the outfitter that has run this stretch for decades.
adventure.bonus: Do the six-hour section and don't check your phone once.

adventure.title: Swim the Springs at Weeki Wachee
adventure.description: A first-magnitude spring pumping 117 million gallons a day of 74-degree water, with a paddle downstream and a swimming area at Buccaneer Bay.
adventure.bonus: Paddle upstream to the spring vent first, then float the whole way back.

adventure.title: Boardwalk Through Lettuce Lake Park
adventure.description: A raised cypress boardwalk over a floodplain on the Hillsborough River, with an observation tower and alligators that are genuinely easy to spot.
adventure.bonus: Climb the tower and stay up there until you see something move.

adventure.title: Snorkel Three Sisters Springs
adventure.description: The only place in the United States where you can legally swim in open water with wild manatees, in a spring-fed cove north of the city.
adventure.bonus: Float completely still on the surface and let one come to you.

adventure.title: Rapids and Suspension Bridge at Hillsborough River State Park
adventure.description: One of Florida's original state parks, with a genuine set of Class II rapids — rare in a state this flat — crossed by a 1930s CCC suspension bridge.
adventure.bonus: Stand in the middle of the swinging bridge until someone else wants past.

adventure.title: Ride Iron Gwazi at Busch Gardens
adventure.description: North America's tallest hybrid coaster: a 206-foot drop at 76mph on a steel track bolted to the bones of an old wooden ride.
adventure.bonus: Ride it once in the front row and once in the back and pick a side.

adventure.title: Sunrise Paddle at Ballast Point
adventure.description: Push off from the little park under the pier in South Tampa and paddle out onto flat bay water with the skyline going pink behind you.
adventure.bonus: Be on the water before the sun clears the horizon. No exceptions.
